blocks.text: Emergency Fire Evacuation Plan Design & Drawings in UAE

Photoluminescent Evacuation Plans,3d evacuation plan,office evacuation plan for Low-Visibility and Power-Outage Compliance.Fire Escape Plans and Emergency Exit Plans Across Abu Dhabi, Dubai, Sharjah and Al Ain

Protect your people and stay compliant with UAE Civil Defence requirements. Firestone Fire & Safety Systems has been designing certified evacuation plans, floor plans, and emergency exit plans since 2007, with Category A approvals from ADCD, DCD, SCD, and SIRA across Abu Dhabi, Dubai, Sharjah, and Al Ain. From detailed 2D layouts to fully isometric 3D drawings, we also design photoluminescent evacuation plans — glow-in-the-dark signage built for low-visibility and power-outage conditions — so every plan meets code and gets your building through inspection the first time, for commercial, residential, and industrial properties alike.
Why Every Building Needs a Certified Evacuation Plan

A clear evacuation plan isn't just a compliance checkbox — it's what gets people out safely during an emergency. UAE Civil Defence authorities (ADCD, DCD, SCD, and Hassantuk-linked SIRA requirements) mandate approved evacuation plans and floor layouts for occupied buildings, and outdated or missing exit plans are one of the most common reasons for failed inspections. Firestone, as a fire and safety company, has been designing and installing evacuation plans since 2007, with Category A approvals across all four emirates we serve.

blocks.text: Everything you need to know about evacuation plan design in the UAE

items.q: Is an evacuation plan legally required in the UAE?
items.a: Yes. UAE Civil Defence authorities require occupied buildings to display an approved evacuation plan as part of fire safety compliance.

items.q: How long does it take to get an evacuation plan designed?
items.a: Turnaround depends on building size and complexity, but standard layouts are typically completed within a few working days of the site assessment.

items.q: Do you provide evacuation plans for construction sites?
items.a: Yes, we design evacuation layouts for active construction sites as well as completed buildings.

items.q: What's the difference between a 2D and 3D evacuation plan?
items.a: A 2D plan is a flat, top-down layout showing exits and routes. A 3D plan uses an isometric view, which many building occupants find easier to read at a glance, especially in complex or multi-floor buildings.

items.q: Do you handle Civil Defence submission and approval?
items.a: Yes, our plans are prepared to meet ADCD, DCD, and SCD documentation standards to support your approval process.
